solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grass cutter's absence from work not welcome

indicators.note: not welcome means the greeting is left out of the longer phrase

parts.note: time off when ill is sick leave
ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: Someone's time off from work is not welcomed, with a gardening tool thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AVE from SICKLEAVE. The 's of 'cutter's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved hand blade traditionally used for reaping crops and lopping long grass.

clue.text: Cab ranks supply eatery

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb, supplely, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Taxi ranks provide a place to grab a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is read as 'in a supple way', the anagram signal for CAB RANKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter serving quick light meals is a small casual place to eat.

clue.text: Dispute working with Paris policeman in court

indicators.note: in places the working policeman within the court letters

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
flic is French slang for a cop

explanation.surface: A row involving a French officer on duty ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Flic is everyday French slang for a police officer, hence 'Paris policeman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash or quarrel between opposing sides is a disagreement, a synonym for dispute.

clue.text: Ignore odd features of blues and heavy metal

indicators.note: skip the odd-numbered letters of the two words and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: A music fan is told to overlook the strange aspects of blues and heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' looks like a music genre alongside blues, but it is the definition, the dense element.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey element Pb is a notably dense metal, used in weights and roofing.

clue.text: A doctor with child seen in clip joint

indicators.note: seen in means these pieces appear inside the clipping word

parts.note: to lop is to clip or trim off
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor and a youngster turn up at a sleazy nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip joint' reads as a seedy bar, but 'clip' gives LOP and 'joint' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat from a young sheep, chop being a piece of meat on the bone, is a joint.

clue.text: The jerk is immersed in same corrupt art movement

indicators.note: immersed in means the jerk phrase sinks into the middle of the rearranged letters
corrupt means the word same is spoiled into a different order

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A sleazy figure is caught up in a decadent artistic school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The jerk' reads as an insult for a person, but splits into THE plus a twitch; 'corrupt' makes AESM, which surrounds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The late-Victorian cult of art for art's sake, championed by Wilde, prized beauty above morals.

clue.text: Dispirited racehorse kicked up racket

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling low

indicators.note: kicked up means the horse's name is turned upwards, read from bottom to top in this down light

parts.note: Red Rum was the famous three-time Grand National winner

explanation.surface: A downcast horse lashes out and causes a din.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is a celebrated British steeplechaser; 'kicked up' turns REDRUM into MURDER. To scream blue murder is to make a great outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a loud fuss or outcry, as in screaming at the top of one's voice.

clue.text: PM once squeezed large Whitehall department

indicators.note: squeezed means the former premier holds the large letter tightly inside

parts.note: Edward Heath was UK Prime Minister in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister shrank a big government ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British Conservative Prime Minister, 1970-74. Whitehall is the London street of government ministries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Department of Health is a UK government ministry, so its short name stands for the department.

clue.text: Short story writer to attempt different style

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote celebrated short stories
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: A writer of short fiction sets out to try a new manner of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an abbreviation signal, but it belongs to 'Short story writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is a style of writing distinct from prose, so it is a different style.

clue.text: Greek hero came in because every second counted

indicators.note: only every second letter of the phrase is counted, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A legendary hero arrived on the scene because each moment mattered.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a Trojan, he is a hero of Greek and Roman legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince of Homer's Iliad and Virgil's Aeneid is a hero of classical Greek myth.

clue.text: Foreign consulate (name withheld) to make oral contact

indicators.note: foreign means the remaining letters are made strange, put in another order
withheld means the name letter is kept back from the word

explanation.surface: An overseas diplomatic office, refusing to give its name, gets in touch by voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withheld' drops N from CONSULATE, and 'Foreign' rearranges the rest. 'oral contact' sounds like a phone call but means a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal, jocular word meaning to kiss, which is contact by mouth.

clue.text: Andes crumbling in SA discovered to be secure

indicators.note: in places the crumbled range inside the word for discovered

parts.note: something discovered has been found

indicators.note: crumbling means the mountains' name breaks up into a new order

explanation.surface: Mountains crumble in South Africa, yet something is found to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: SA stays as written; 'crumbling' turns ANDES into EANDS, which goes 'in' FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Unharmed and out of danger, the idiom describes someone safe from all harm.

clue.text: Family gathers round large cooker

indicators.note: gathers round means the family word surrounds the large letter

parts.note: kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Relatives crowd around a big stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace for firing pottery or drying grain, a jocular stretch of an oven or cooker.

clue.text: Cheater fiddled with MOT instrument

indicators.note: fiddled means the letters are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheat rigged a car's roadworthiness test with a gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A rev counter showing engine speed is a measuring dial or gauge, an instrument.

clue.text: Invoice blogger for sticker?

parts.note: a bill is an invoice
a blogger is one who posts online

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an online writer sending invoices is a persistent type.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pastes up notices on walls sticks things up, so the question mark flags a whimsical sense.

clue.text: Piano work each recruit played, maintaining tempo

indicators.note: maintaining means the rearranged letters keep the tempo letter held within
played means the words are performed in a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tempo

explanation.surface: A pianist plays a piece while every newcomer keeps time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' is Renzo Piano, the Italian architect, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Renzo Piano designs buildings, so his output is the design of buildings.

clue.text: Fashionista hosting a doctor's part of circle

indicators.note: hosting means the designer's name holds the others as guests within

parts.note: Mary Quant was the designer who popularised the miniskirt
DR is the abbreviation for doctor, the 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A fashion figure plays host to a doctor's social set.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was a British fashion designer of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of a circle, the sector bounded by two radii at right angles.

clue.text: Rose climbs here, displaying pearlies

indicators.note: displaying means the letters are spread out and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose climbs up showing off her pearly costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as a woman's name but is the flower. Pearlies are the pearl-button suits of London's Pearly Kings and Queens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice or frame against a wall that trains fruit trees or climbing plants to grow flat.

clue.text: They offer freedom to ignore draughts without king

parts.note: to blank someone is to ignore them

indicators.note: without means the king letter is removed from the game's name

parts.note: chequers is a name for the board game draughts
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Players set free to disregard the board game once the king is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Signed orders to pay with the amount left open give the holder free rein to spend.

clue.text: It qualifies action subtly, for example

definitions.meaning: a word that modifies a verb
subtly is an instance of this part of speech

explanation.surface: Something finely modifies what is done, as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A part of speech modifying a verb, of which a word ending in -ly like 'subtly' is a typical case.

clue.text: Judge Jenny?

definitions.meaning: a jenny is a female donkey, jokingly an ass with the feminine ending -ess

explanation.walkthrough: A jenny is a female donkey; adding the feminine suffix -ess to 'ass' gives a playful word for her, as in lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or weigh up is to judge; the second sense is a mock feminine of donkey.

clue.text: Gangs in Norfolk town strip

indicators.note: in places the gangs inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
posses are bands or gangs

explanation.surface: Gangs in an East Anglian town strip people of their goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small town in Norfolk, an English county; the gangs sit 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone of land or property is to strip them of it.

clue.text: Reside abroad, going over plan

indicators.note: the answer goes over the gap between the two words, straddling them

explanation.surface: Someone proposes living overseas and reviews the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' and 'going over' suggest an anagram or reversal, but the letters sit in order across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or scheme in mind, such as a proposal, is a plan.

clue.text: Knight had forgotten banquet

indicators.note: forgotten means the word had is left out of the knight's name

parts.note: Sir Galahad is the Round Table knight

explanation.surface: A knight forgot about a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive celebration or grand party, such as a gala dinner, is a lavish feast.

clue.text: Busy outlet stops fuel distribution

indicators.note: stops means the outlet plugs the gap inside the shuffled letters
distribution means the letters of fuel are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: a vent is an outlet for air or gas

explanation.surface: A busy outlet halts the supply of petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlet' tempts as a shop, but it is an opening for air; 'distribution' makes EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A day full of happenings or incidents is a busy one.

clue.text: Compiler's regretfully sent back seasoned dish

indicators.note: sent back means the phrase is returned, read from the end

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; 'compiler's' is 'compiler is', I'm
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A setter sadly returns a spicy dish to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler's' stands for 'I'm' (the setter is), giving IM ALAS, then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced, cured Italian sausage, served sliced, is a highly flavoured dish.

clue.text: Get on website regularly blocking "The Woman in White"

indicators.note: blocking means the picked letters plug the middle of the woman's word

parts.note: a bride is a woman dressed in white

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of website is taken

explanation.surface: Someone goes online regularly to read the Wilkie Collins novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Woman in White is a Wilkie Collins novel; here it is a bride. EST, the even letters, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit astride a horse or bicycle is to get on it with legs either side.

clue.text: Two queens, one over time a victim of her faith

indicators.note: one over means one of the queens covers time, closing round it

parts.note: Mary is a queen's name and R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Two queens, one reigning over an era, and one died for her beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside MARY, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone killed for refusing to renounce their religion is the classic sufferer for belief.
